tagline: A loop through the oak and cherry, around a contested lake.
intro: The loop starts where Longhouse Drive meets Route 321 and climbs through hardwoods and hemlock toward the top of the plateau, under oak and black cherry, where the road can feel like a tunnel. Route 59 takes it past the Rimrock turnoff down to the reservoir, across Cornplanter Bridge, and back around the Kinzua Creek arm on Longhouse Drive, 36 miles in all.

The lake came late. Kinzua Dam made it in 1965, and the hamlets of Kinzua and Cornplanter were lost, with some of the Seneca Nation's land flooded. Its unofficial name, Lake Perfidy, comes from a Peter La Farge ballad that Johnny Cash recorded.

moments.title: Old Powerhouse
moments.text: A scrap-metal powerhouse from 1939 drove the rod lines to the oil pumps for half a century, in country where the Bradford field once supplied over 90 percent of the nation's petroleum.

moments.title: Jakes Rocks Overlook
moments.text: Hardened paths wander through the woods, past trees growing through the boulders, to a rock outcrop looking over Jackson Bay, Kinzua Dam and the forest beyond.
